newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan banks may join $6 bln Thai loan package-Jiji.
newsitem.headline: Japan banks may join $6 bln Thai loan package-Jiji.

text.p: Major Japanese banks and banks from other countries are considering extending loans of around $6 billion to Thailand to help ease its economic woes, Jiji news agency reported on Friday.
Jiji quoted banking sources as saying that such assistance would be dependent on the International Monetary Fund (IMF) also providing loans to Thailand.
The banks' loan package would likely be dispersed in late September, when the IMF and the World Bank are due to hold their annual joint meeting in Hong Kong, Jiji quoted the sources as saying.

Although there had been no formal requests as yet from the Thai government, the sources said they expected Thailand to ask for loans from private banks after the decision on the IMF package, Jiji said.
The private banks likely to join in the package are Japanese, U.S. and European banks which have offices in Thailand and some Asian banks as well, the report said.
Japanese banks, including Sakura Bank Ltd, would likely provide about half the package, it said.
Japan's Ministry of Finance said it was unaware of the banks' loan plan.

A spokesman for Sakura Bank said the bank had not received a request for funds from the Thai government and could not in any case take any such action while Thailand was still negotiating with the IMF.
